title: pm-dispatch: area-lease mode for any lane — dynamic areas, review seats, land-after-PASS, Tier H hand-off, cross-account GitHub handover (from the #33059 pilot)
body:
domain:server#6 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cztR1A2CZoxSZyuoGP

Filing gate: ③ a maintainer-directed task. Maintainer's words (project thread, 2026-11-15, verbatim): 「然后应该立卡更新skills。这种方式适合推广到其他车道吗？」 · 「所以是否分区域，如何分区域应该是动态的是吗？」 · 「你直接立卡，然后让 server 5 按照你的卡处理也可以」.

## 维护者速读

- 把 #33059 server 区域租约试点的做法写进 pm-dispatch 技能，让每个车道都能用：一个席位、按需分区、复审席位、复审通过后区域自己落地。
- 分不分区、分几个区、边界怎么划，都由席位动态决定：坐席时定，每次交接或换班时复核。
- 证据：试点约 18 小时里关闭 117 张 server 卡（p1 12、p2 69），合并 106 个区域 PR；试点前两个 24 小时窗口分别关 58、50 张。用量 14%→84%，约每 1% 关 1.7 张卡。
- 在技能 PR 合并之前，server seat 5（新账号）按本卡 §2 的工作方案执行。

## 1. Pilot evidence (#33059, 2026-11-14 14:30Z → 2026-11-15 09:00Z)

| Measure | Value |
|:--|:--|
| `domain:server` issues closed | **117** (p1 12, p2 69, rest p3/other) |
| Area PRs merged (`head:claude/area-*`) | **106** |
| Same metric, the two prior 24 h windows | 58 and 50 closed |
| Open `domain:server` issues created before the pilot | 181 at start → 95 still open |
| Weekly usage on the running account | 14% (16:18Z) → 38% → 52% → 61% → 73% → 83% → 84% (08:39Z); ≈ 1.7 cards closed per 1% |
| Merge-queue failures | 28 of 293 queue runs in the first ~11 h; each failure rebuilds every group behind it, so queue duty was added |

Shape that worked: 1 seat + 8 areas (A1–A5, E1, E2, E2b) + 3 review seats; up to 4 sub-agents per area; areas land after PASS; seat keeps W0, rulings, Tier H, ledger.

Failures and lessons (each needs a line in the skill):
1. **Tier H hand-off missed.** Several governed PRs sat as drafts with a PASS but no ACCEPT / `pr_ready` / `pm:awaiting-merge` / `pr_request_reviewers`, so the maintainer could not see them. Fix: every seat round re-checks every PASS'd governed PR for the four-piece hand-off.
2. **Mailbox not opened at the pilot's seating** ("drop the old rules" was read as "no mailbox"), so triage's knocks went nowhere for a day. Fix: the mailbox step is never dropped; re-seating or moving seats opens a new one.
3. **Account handover in local files only.** The next account (different login) cannot read project files or memory. Fix: the seat's handover and each area's state go into a GitHub comment on the seat post.
4. **Overlap between two accounts.** The outgoing account kept draining while the new one started. Fix: an explicit ownership split on the seat post. The outgoing account moves to a free seat with its own mailbox and posts "ownership transferred" when done.
5. **A measured gain was wrong.** A benchmark headline was taken without the security chain the engine really emits. Review caught it before filing. Fix: perf cards quote numbers from the reviewed bench PR only.
6. **Claim label writes silently missing** on one card. Fix: read the labels back after a claim.
7. **Context/token cost.** Coordination threads that read diffs/logs burned context. Fix: all code reading goes to sub-agents; coordination threads rotate at ~150k.

## 2. The work plan (seat 5 runs this until the skill lands)

### 2.1 Goal
Full-speed `domain:server` p1 + p2. Epic #33631 (SQL performance) children are part of the p1/p2 pool. p3 only as a same-file ride-along (≤5 cards/PR, ≤~100 lines, no Clause-② answer of its own).

### 2.2 Dynamic partitioning (new rule)
- **At seating, and again at every handover or shift**, the seat decides:
  - whether to split into areas at all: split when the open p1/p2 count and the number of independent module clusters they touch justify more than one parallel session (rule of thumb: ≥15 claimable p1/p2 cards across ≥3 clusters);
  - how many areas;
  - their boundaries: group by the files and packages the cards touch, so two areas rarely edit the same function.
- **Merge** areas whose queue is drained; **split** an area that backs up.
- **Review seats scale with active areas:** about 1 per 3 active areas. One owns merge-queue duty.
- The lease table (area → paths → thread → reviewer) lives in the seat post and is rewritten whenever it changes.
- The 2026-11-14 server split, as a starting point to re-derive, not a fixed rule:
  - A1 plugin-auth
  - A2 plugin-security / audit / email / notify / Setup metadata
  - A3 storage / attachments / approvals / trash / analytics + dataset routes
  - A4 drivers / seed loader / formula / objectql filter compile / schema sync / health
  - A5 runtime (not action routes) / hono server / automation / cli / packaging
  - E1 metadata-protocol (protocol.ts serial)
  - E2 security catalog / webhooks / metadata history + loader
  - E2b runtime action routes / objectql function holders

### 2.3 Startup
1. Seat session takes the seat: seat post stub, **own mailbox** (`scripts/pm/mailbox-open.mjs --seat LANE#N --login L`; in a cloud container push the session's branch and pass `--head`), lease table, start comment on the pilot/epic card.
2. One project thread per area and per review seat.
3. **The maintainer writes one authorising line in each new thread.** Auto mode accepts only the maintainer's own words in the acting thread; relayed copies and card taps do not count.
   - Area threads: 「本区通过复审的 PR 都可以 ready + auto-merge」
   - Seat thread: 「审批人批准后的 Tier H PR 你可以自主落地」
4. W0 in each area's first hour: a close / fold / regrade / decision list to the seat. The seat writes after the maintainer sees it. Start the first p1 at once.

### 2.4 Working rules
- **Claim:** re-read labels, assignee and last comment first. Do not touch a card with another assignee, a `Claim:` comment, or a `lease:*` that is not just an epic area tag. Then one `label-write.mjs` stroke (`pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` + `lease:<ID>` + assignee) and a `Claim:` comment naming `claude/area-<ID>-<card>` (`check:closing-target-claim` needs it). Read the labels back. Open the draft PR at the first push.
- **Development:** all code via `os-dev` sub-agents (worktree, one card or coupled set each, file-disjoint). At most 4 in development per area, cut to 2–3 when usage runs fast. Land built PRs before starting new cards. Pre-push runs tests for the touched packages plus their dependents, typecheck and lint. A PR touching a shared package (spec, objectql, runtime, metadata, metadata-protocol, plugin-security, rest, core) runs its direct dependents and regenerates pinned baselines on current main before arming.
- **Review:**
  - The area sends `PR #N · area · Fixes … · head <sha>` to its reviewer and leaves a `Request: review` PR comment.
  - Reviewers post the claim line, then PASS/FAIL. Clause-② yes ⇒ a full contract-review record.
  - Self-review is allowed only for text, comment or test-pin PRs. Areas with no hot red-line surface may also self-review ≤50-line Clause-② no PRs.
  - A clean main merge (same patch-id) keeps the PASS. A resolved conflict needs a delta review.
- **Landing (area):**
  1. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr N`.
  2. Checks are green on the head.
  3. ACCEPT comment.
  4. Relay `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`.
  5. Follow it to MERGED.
- **Tier H (governed):** the seat hands off in one stroke:
  1. ACCEPT comment
  2. `pr_ready`
  3. `pm:awaiting-merge` label
  4. `pr_request_reviewers` os-zhuang, hotlong and the maintainer
  On an APPROVED review from os-zhuang or hotlong, the seat arms it.
- **Merge queue:** the queue-duty reviewer classifies every merge_group failure within 15 min as flake, conflict or infra, and routes it. The seat jumps a PR that fixes a signature ejecting others with `pr_enqueue_front` (audit comment first, one per repo, never re-sent on failure). Builds are set to 20; drop to 15 if runs time out or exceed 50 min.
- **Rulings:** a seat ruling that changes observable behaviour or interprets an ADR gets one independent review first. Routing (split, fold, defer, area) needs none. Maintainer decisions are framed as short business-terms options with a recommendation.
- **Seat inbox:** decisions, Tier H to land, security (never on GitHub), cross-area file conflicts, blockers and HANDOVER DONE only.
- **Context and quota:** rotate a thread at ~150k context at a clean point (never mid-review). At each usage reading, log %, cards closed and PRs merged.
- **At ~80% usage, HANDOVER:**
  1. No new dispatch of any priority.
  2. Let current pushes finish and put every branch in a draft PR.
  3. Write the handover on GitHub: the seat post comment carries ownership, open PRs and next steps, pending approvals and traps.

### 2.5 Ownership during overlap (current)
os-elon-musk drains from domain:server seat 6 (#29908, mailbox PR #33750). It holds the PRs listed in https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/28677#issuecomment-6891900284 until it posts "ownership transferred" on #28677. Seat 5 takes only the free set listed there.

## 3. Skill changes (the deliverable)
- `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/` gains an "area-lease mode" reference covering:
  - §2.2 dynamic partitioning
  - §2.3 startup, including the authorising-line step
  - §2.4 rules
  - the cross-account GitHub handover and ownership split
  - the Tier H four-piece re-check every round
  - the mailbox-on-every-seating rule
- `seat-lifecycle.md`: moving seats with your own mailbox and an "ownership transferred" comment, for an account that keeps draining while another takes its seat.
- `lanes/*.md`: one line naming area-lease mode as available to any lane whose open p1/p2 backlog crosses the split threshold.
- Generalisation: nothing here is server-specific except the example split. Other lanes derive their own areas from their card/file map.

## Reader
domain:server#5 (zhuangjianguo) runs §2 now. The skills lane (or seat 5, if the maintainer says so) writes §3 as one PR. Tier H: the skill tree is governed, so the PR needs os-zhuang or hotlong approval.

## Dedupe
`repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue area-lease skill` → only #33059 (the pilot card) and seat posts. No skill card exists.
